advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the degrade re-read uses the same criterion-id set the primary banked against (or key the surfaced finding off the bank entry directly) so a genuine banked BLOCK is never silently downgraded to an unverified placeholder on ticket drift.
evidence: completion_recovery.py:211 `ticket = _reads.show_ticket(ticket_id, repo_root=ctx.repo_root)` — an independent re-read from the primary's banking read

completion_banking.py:180-182 `norm = re.sub(...).casefold(); h = hashlib.sha256(norm.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]; return f"c{index:02d}-{h}"` — id identity is derived from criterion text, so drift changes ids
completion_verdict_assembly.py:91-93 `for text in criteria: cid = ids[text]; entry = bank_entries.get(cid)` — a mismatched cid yields None and falls to the placeholder branch (lines 119-139)
advisory.finding: The degrade re-reads the ticket in _expected_criteria and recomputes criterion ids (criterion_id_map -> mint_criterion_id, which hashes normalized criterion text). If the ticket's criteria text drifted between the primary run (which banked under one id set) and this degrade read, the banked actionable BLOCK's criterion_id will not match any recomputed cid, and assemble_deterministic_verdict will render that criterion as an unverified met=false placeholder rather than surfacing the genuine banked refutation — the specific operator-actionable finding is silently lost (the degrade still returns a FAIL). Same drift risk exists in the pre-existing _recover path, so it is not newly introduced by this diff.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that injects a fault (e.g. monkeypatch bank.all or assemble_deterministic_verdict to raise) while an actionable BLOCK is banked, asserting the outage LLMUnavailableError re-raises.
evidence: completion_recovery.py:194-200: `except Exception:  # best-effort: any fault falls through to the caller's re-raise (exit-11)` ... `return None`

Docstring completion_recovery.py:164-166: 'any fault (a bank read error, an unreadable ticket) logs at WARN and returns None so the caller re-raises the outage — the degrade is an enhancement, never a new failure mode on the outage path.'

ABSENCE: search of the test file for 'Exception' and '_degrade_from_actionable_bank' returns no matches; no scenario forces bank.all() or assemble_deterministic_verdict to raise while an actionable block is banked.

Named violating input: an actionable-block bank (met=false, evidence_sufficient absent) where bank.all() or assemble_deterministic_verdict raises RuntimeError — the contract requires the original LLMUnavailableError to propagate.
advisory.finding: The documented best-effort guard in _degrade_from_actionable_bank (the `except Exception` arm that must fall through to re-raise the outage so the degrade is 'never a new failure mode') is untested. No test injects a fault during the degrade attempt with an actionable-block bank to verify the outage LLMUnavailableError is re-raised rather than swallowed or converted into a different failure.
scenarios: A bank-store read error or an assembly error occurs after an actionable BLOCK was banked and an outage fired; the guard must re-raise LLMUnavailableError (exit-11), not surface a new failure mode.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case using the actionable bank_action but monkeypatch _bank.assemble_deterministic_verdict (or bank.all) to raise, then assert pytest.raises(LLMUnavailableError) and that no verdict StepResult was returned.
